title: Three interventions to investigate
description: These proposals use exact precomputed comparisons from the supplied fixed atrium model. They are prompts for design and review, not predictions for edits made to an uploaded model.

ideas.title: Investigate an external roof screen
ideas.summary: Explore a removable or retractable screen above the glazed atrium roof, starting with a 50% opacity reference case.
ideas.proposalStatus: Evidence-backed concept; not an approved intervention

applicability.referenceModel: Geoffrey Manton atrium — organiser fixed EnergyPlus room
applicability.geometryChangePolicy: Keep this reference separate. A new model or edited geometry requires a separately completed analysis and explicit scope statement before reporting its performance.
applicability.parameterScope: Five supplied levers on the organiser fixed atrium; roof screening is the script-defined added shade, not arbitrary replacement geometry.

benefits: The exact 50% screen reference reduces the supplied heat score from 320.6 to 121.5 K·h and peak operative temperature from 40.47 to 35.28°C.
The screen lever can be explored without changing the existing glazing g-value or U-value in this reference model.
tradeoffs: The starter daylight proxy retains 50% of its baseline value; this is a proxy, not a Radiance daylight result.
The 50% case remains above the 42 K·h event target.
The winter glazing-conduction proxy is unchanged, but winter solar gains, lighting energy and full annual heating demand were not assessed.
checksBeforeApplying: Confirm roof load paths, fixing permissions, wind uplift and maintenance access with the relevant specialists.
Verify fire, drainage, cleaning and roof access requirements.
Develop real screen geometry, product transmittance and an operating schedule before calculating a proposed design.

reversibility.label: Potentially removable or retractable
reversibility.details: A separable screen may permit removal, but fixings, penetrations, access and restoration need review; reversibility is not established by the sweep.

calculationLimits: Each supplied case uses a constant-transmittance horizontal screen at z=24.5 m with a 2 m perimeter margin. It does not simulate a retracting mechanism, hourly controls or arbitrary screen geometry.
The night-zero counterpart is row 2177: 183.5 K·h, peak 36.42°C, with all other levers unchanged.

ideas.title: Investigate controlled night ventilation
ideas.summary: Explore whether night ventilation could discharge stored heat while retaining the existing glazing and roof appearance.
ideas.proposalStatus: Evidence-backed concept; not an approved intervention

applicability.referenceModel: Geoffrey Manton atrium — organiser fixed EnergyPlus room
applicability.geometryChangePolicy: Keep this reference separate. A new model or edited geometry requires a separately completed analysis and explicit scope statement before reporting its performance.
applicability.parameterScope: Five supplied levers on the organiser fixed atrium; roof screening is the script-defined added shade, not arbitrary replacement geometry.

benefits: Changing night ventilation from 1 to 6 ACH gives 235.9 K·h and a 39.27°C peak, compared with 320.6 K·h and 40.47°C at baseline.
Daylight and winter glazing-conduction proxies remain unchanged because glazing and screening are unchanged.
tradeoffs: This intervention alone remains above the 42 K·h event target.
Achieving 6 ACH is not guaranteed by opening a window; real free area, airflow, noise, rain, security and controls require review.
Fans, controls, maintenance energy and year-round ventilation heat loss are not included in the quoted proxies.
checksBeforeApplying: Confirm available inlet/outlet locations and free opening areas without assuming grey objects can be altered.
Check security, rain, acoustic, smoke-control and operating requirements.
Validate achievable airflow and controls with an appropriate airflow model and commissioning plan.

reversibility.label: Operational changes may be reversible
reversibility.details: A control schedule can be changed, but new vents, actuators or structural openings may create lasting alterations and require separate approval.

calculationLimits: The source models prescribed air changes as Honeybee infiltration schedules, not flow through actual openings or a tested purge-control system.
The night-zero counterpart is row 2175: 470.3 K·h, peak 42.23°C; this changes the entire modelled schedule including warm-up.

ideas.title: Investigate solar-control glazing during replacement
ideas.summary: Compare lower solar gain and improved glazing insulation together, while checking daylight and real product availability.
ideas.proposalStatus: Evidence-backed concept; not an approved intervention

benefits: The g=0.35, U=1.6 reference gives 172.7 K·h and a 36.64°C peak, against baseline g=0.6, U=2.8 at 320.6 K·h and 40.47°C.
The simplified winter glazing-conduction proxy falls by 42.9%; this is not a whole-building energy or bill saving.
tradeoffs: The starter daylight proxy retains 58.3% of baseline; spectral glazing properties and detailed daylight must be checked.
The case still exceeds the event heat target and remains dependent on operating assumptions.
Replacement glazing entails installation, access and material impacts that the source dataset does not quantify.
checksBeforeApplying: Find available glazing systems with verified g-value, U-value and visible-light transmittance; independent grid settings are not a product catalogue.
Review frames, supports, seals, condensation and thermal bridges rather than treating the pane as the whole facade.
Assess detailed daylight, glare, annual energy, embodied impacts and replacement sequence before selection.

reversibility.label: Material replacement with lasting consequences
reversibility.details: Glazing replacement can involve removal, waste and changes to frames or seals. A recovery or replacement plan would need to be designed.

calculationLimits: The combined comparison changes both g-value and U-value; its benefit must not be attributed to insulation alone.
In the supplied insulation-only reference (g=0.6, U=1.6), score rises to 418.7 K·h and peak to 41.94°C.

The EnergyPlus simple-glazing construction uses a fixed visible transmittance of 0.7; the separate daylight proxy assumes visible transmittance scales with g-value. Neither is a verified product result.
The night-zero counterpart is row 800: 290.8 K·h, peak 38.27°C.

limitations: Supplied precomputed simulations, not live Grasshopper results or sensor measurements.
These results apply to the organiser’s fixed single-zone atrium and source shading context; they do not validate an uploaded or edited model.
The room is well mixed, its lower surrounding boundaries are adiabatic, and fixed air-change schedules do not resolve flow through real openings.
One crude 2050 weather morph is represented; there is no climate ensemble or demonstrated climate robustness.
A night-zero comparison changes the complete simulated schedule, including warm-up, not one isolated failed night.
Daylight, winter glazing heat loss and opening area are proxies; cost, carbon, structural adequacy and product feasibility were not computed.
The event score target is not regulatory compliance or a certificate of safe temperature.
Independent glazing g/U settings and idealised roof screens are analytical inputs, not verified products.
